passages.original: ludi quam amplissimi ut fierent senatus decrevit. ad eos ludos auctore Attio Tullio vis magna Volscorum venit. priusquam committerentur ludi, Tullius, ut domi compositum cum Marcio fuerat, ad consules venit; dicit esse quae secreto agere de re publica velit. arbitris remotis invitus , inquit, quod sequius sit de meis civibus loquor.
passages.english: The senate decreed that the games should be held on the grandest possible scale. At the instigation of Attius Tullius a great crowd of Volscians came to these games. Before the games began, Tullius, as had been arranged at home with Marcius, came to the consuls; he said there were matters concerning the state that he wished to discuss in private. When the witnesses had been removed, he said: "It is against my will that I say something to the discredit of my own fellow citizens."
passages.notes: "quod sequius sit": literally "what is rather worse", i.e. something unfavourable.
